statement: Bootstrapping or repairing a Sergeant installation must be interactive and idempotent: orchestrate only supported commands, and surface any missing capability as a separate tracked issue rather than inventing an undocumented workaround.
trigger: the user asks to install, configure, or repair Sergeant
outcome: the setup procedure only performs supported operations and every gap becomes tracked work
notes: Top-of-file mission statement for the whole skill.
rationale: Defines a recognizable trigger (install/repair) and bounded outcome (supported-only actions, gaps tracked) independent of any single stage; satisfies the §6.2 reusable-procedure test.
alternatives_considered: agents-invariant (rejected: scoped to one skill's operating mode, not a system-wide rule)

statement: sergeant-setup should be loaded when the user wants to install/configure Sergeant for the first time, register a new project or add repositories to an existing one, diagnose/repair a broken or incomplete installation, or verify that an existing setup is working.
trigger: one of the four listed user intents is present
outcome: the correct workflow is selected
rationale: Trigger enumeration for the workflow, per the §6.2 test.

statement: sergeant-setup must not be loaded for documentation-only questions or questions about a specific command; those route to sergeant-help instead.
trigger: the request is informational rather than an install/repair action
outcome: the read-only help workflow is used instead of the mutating setup workflow
notes: Direct workflow-boundary evidence between sergeant-setup and sergeant-help.
rationale: Establishes a negative trigger that keeps two candidate workflows (setup vs help) distinct rather than merged.

statement: sergeant-setup is permitted to write only to Sergeant-owned paths: the global config at ~/.config/sergeant/config.yaml and per-project YAML files at ~/.config/sergeant/<project>.yaml.
trigger: any step of sergeant-setup is about to write a file
outcome: writes stay confined to Sergeant's own config namespace
rationale: A durable write-scope invariant that governs every phase of the workflow, not one checkpoint; represented as workflow-wide context rather than a new stage.
alternatives_considered: agents-invariant (rejected: the path allowlist is specific to this skill's writes, not a system-wide rule)

statement: sergeant-setup must never write to other tools' configuration surfaces (opencode config, ~/.claude or any repository's CLAUDE.md/.claude, Codex config, Goose config, any repository's AGENTS.md/.github) or to any path outside ~/.config/sergeant/ that the user did not explicitly name.
trigger: any step of sergeant-setup is about to write a file
outcome: other tools' and repositories' configuration remains untouched
notes: Enumerates negative space precisely by tool and path, not just 'be careful'.
rationale: Same class as the prior write-scope unit: a workflow-wide boundary the actor must hold across every phase.

statement: td, Graphify, and Treehouse are never auto-initialized by sergeant-setup; each requires an explicit confirmation prompt before any command runs, and if consent is declined the state is left unchanged and the skip is reported.
trigger: a phase would initialize an optional external tool
outcome: no optional external tool is initialized without explicit per-tool consent
rationale: A workflow-wide consent policy that recurs at Phases 7-9; kept as shared workflow context rather than duplicated per phase.
alternatives_considered: shared-context across skills: this consent-before-mutation shape recurs in cross-repo-work, dispatch, and load-project; flagged as a @@consent-gate shared-context candidate in notes rather than claimed here to avoid inventing the convention's scope prematurely.

statement: sergeant-setup maintains a visible numbered checklist: before each step it verifies whether the step is already complete and skips it without prompting if so; after each step it writes an [ok] or [skipped] status line; when a phase fails, the run stops with actionable output identifying the last completed phase.
trigger: the workflow is running
outcome: the operator always sees exact progress and the exact failure point
rationale: Defines the workflow's own checkpoint/reporting shape across all phases -- itself evidence that each numbered phase is a meaningful durable checkpoint (the §6.3 test) rather than incidental script structure.

statement: Re-running sergeant-setup after a partial run restarts the checklist from Phase 1 but skips every phase that already passes verification; resumability works by re-checking each phase before acting, not by persisting run state between invocations.
trigger: sergeant-setup is invoked again after a prior partial or complete run
outcome: the run converges to the same end state without redoing completed work or persisting extra state
notes: Explicit design choice: verification-before-action substitutes for a persisted resume pointer.
rationale: This resumability requirement is fully expressible by an actor stage that inspects current state each time it runs; it does not require the runtime to own new durable resume state, so it is not promoted to engine-gap.
alternatives_considered: engine-gap (considered and rejected): Work's existing blocked/failed-retry transition table already lets an operator re-invoke a stalled or failed Work, and idempotent-by-re-verification is an ordinary actor-stage judgment call, not a new runtime fact.

statement: Phase 1 classifies every checked prerequisite as present, installable (a supported bootstrap command exists), or unsupported (file a tracked issue).
trigger: Phase 1 (prerequisite detection) runs
outcome: every prerequisite has one of three dispositions before Phase 2 begins
rationale: A three-way classification with a bounded outcome set is exactly the shape of a durable checkpoint: operators would care whether the run blocked here.

statement: Required prerequisites for Sergeant are: bash 3.2+, git, an authenticated gh, tmux, yq, lsof, a td implementation supporting --description/--json/--work-dir, and at least one interactive agent (opencode, goose, or claude).
trigger: Phase 1 runs
outcome: the exact required-tool set for Sergeant to operate is enumerated
notes: The td version constraint (specific supported flags) is itself measured/pinned capability evidence, echoing this repo's own measure-don't-assume doctrine.
rationale: Enumerated content belongs inside the Phase 1 checkpoint's context, not as a separate checkpoint.

statement: Optional prerequisites (mise, treehouse, graphify, no-mistakes, node/npm) are skipped, not failed, when absent.
trigger: Phase 1 runs
outcome: absence of an optional tool never blocks setup
rationale: Distinguishes required from optional dependencies within the same checkpoint.

statement: For each unsupported prerequisite, sergeant-setup drafts a td issue (title, description, acceptance criteria) and shows it for explicit y/yes approval before creating it; on decline it reports the gap in the summary and creates no tracked work.
trigger: a required or optional prerequisite is classified unsupported
outcome: either a tracked issue exists or the gap is explicitly reported, never silently dropped or silently created
rationale: A consent-gated side effect (creating tracked work) subordinate to the Phase 1 checkpoint.

statement: sergeant-setup does not continue past Phase 1 until every required prerequisite is present or the user explicitly accepts the risk of proceeding without it.
trigger: Phase 1 completes its checks
outcome: Phase 2 never begins on an unresolved required-prerequisite gap without explicit risk acceptance
rationale: A hard gate condition on leaving the Phase 1 checkpoint -- confirms Phase 1 is a real durable boundary, not merely informational output.

statement: For each installable prerequisite, sergeant-setup shows the exact installation command and requires explicit y/yes consent before running it; any other response leaves the system unchanged.
trigger: a prerequisite is classified installable
outcome: no installation command runs without explicit per-command consent
rationale: Same consent-before-mutation shape as the unsupported-prerequisite handling, applied to installs instead of issue creation.

statement: When cloning Sergeant, the destination path is asked for explicitly and the workflow waits for the user's answer before doing anything else.
trigger: the Sergeant repository is not already cloned
outcome: a destination is established before any clone attempt
rationale: Part of the Phase 2 (clone/install) checkpoint's required interaction sequence.

statement: The clone command is shown verbatim with the resolved destination and requires explicit y/N consent; any other response leaves the filesystem unchanged.
trigger: a clone destination has been established
outcome: cloning never happens without an explicit, visible, confirmed command
rationale: Consent-before-mutation, same pattern as Phase 1's install/issue gates.

statement: When mise is available, sergeant-setup first resolves the actual install directory from SGT_INSTALL_DIR, defaulting to $HOME/.local/bin.
trigger: mise is present
outcome: the exact install target is known and can be shown to the user before running anything
rationale: Deterministic resolution rule subordinate to the Phase 2 checkpoint.

statement: sergeant-setup shows the resolved install target and requires explicit consent before running mise run install; if mise is unavailable or consent is declined, it instructs the user to symlink bin/ commands onto PATH manually and to verify the result before continuing.
trigger: the install directory has been resolved
outcome: commands are installed only via an explicit consented path or an explicit manual fallback, never silently
rationale: Consent gate plus an explicit fallback path when the primary mechanism is unavailable or declined.

statement: After install, sergeant-setup verifies that at least sgt-list, sgt-context, sgt-dispatch, and sgt-watch resolve on PATH; missing commands and their expected source paths are reported, and the run stops if verification fails, resuming from Phase 2 on the next invocation.
trigger: an install path (mise or manual) has been attempted
outcome: the environment is proven to have the commands the rest of setup depends on, before proceeding
rationale: A concrete, observable completion condition for the Phase 2 checkpoint (the §6.3 'operators would care whether this succeeded' test).

statement: sergeant-setup checks for ~/.config/sergeant/config.yaml; if missing, it asks the user for a dev_root path, then shows a full preview of the file content and requires explicit y/N confirmation before writing anything.
trigger: the global config file does not exist
outcome: the global config is written only after the user has seen and approved its exact content
rationale: Preview-then-confirm pattern, subordinate to the Phase 3 checkpoint.

statement: If the global config is present and valid, sergeant-setup verifies dev_root is set and reports [ok] without further action.
trigger: the global config already exists and parses
outcome: an already-correct global config is left untouched
rationale: The idempotent 'already complete, skip' branch of the Phase 3 checkpoint.

statement: If the global config exists but fails to parse as YAML (checked via yq), sergeant-setup reports the parse error and stops; it never overwrites the file without a timestamped backup, a diff preview, and explicit confirmation.
trigger: the global config exists and is invalid
outcome: an unparseable config is never silently replaced
rationale: A fail-stop branch distinct from both the missing-file and valid-file branches of the same checkpoint.

statement: If the project YAML already exists and the user wants to modify it, Phase 4 (the new-project interview) is skipped entirely in favor of Phase 5 (repair existing YAML).
trigger: a project YAML already exists
outcome: the new-project interview never runs against an existing project
rationale: Defines the branch condition separating two candidate checkpoints (new-project interview vs. repair), showing they are mutually exclusive durable paths.

statement: The new-project interview asks, in strict order and waiting for each answer before proceeding: project name (YAML filename stem, must match [a-z0-9_-]+), per-repository name/path/clone-URL/role/group, per-group description and shared agent_instructions, default agent instructions applied to every repository, project-level GitHub identity, and an optional Graphify output path.
trigger: a new project is being registered
outcome: all information needed to write a complete project YAML has been collected in a fixed order
rationale: The ordered question set is the content of the Phase 4 checkpoint; each question's dependency on the prior answer is what makes 'ask in order, wait for each' load-bearing.

statement: The project interview requires stopping and waiting for each individual answer before asking the next question, for an unbounded-length, data-dependent question set (one round per repository, one round per named group).
trigger: the interview reaches a question whose branching depends on a prior answer (e.g. how many repositories, how many groups)
outcome: each question is asked only after the prior answer is known, and the number of rounds is not fixed in advance
notes: Distinct from the ordinary consent-gate pattern: this is intra-procedure, data-dependent, multi-round human input inside what the current engine models as a single actor-stage turn.
rationale: Every actor stage in the current engine runs one fresh execution per stage and advances only on an explicit BackendSignal from that execution (CLAUDE.md 'Work state != process state'; proposal §3.4). A data-dependent sequence of several separate wait-for-answer rounds inside one stage, where the number of rounds is not known until runtime, cannot be represented as a single bounded actor-stage turn.

engine_gap.behavior: A single stage's procedure must ask the user several separate, sequentially dependent questions (project name, then a variable number of per-repository rounds, then a variable number of per-group rounds, then default instructions, identity, and graphify path), stopping and waiting for each answer before formulating the next question, where the total number of question rounds is not known until the user answers earlier ones.
engine_gap.source_evidence: sergeant-setup/SKILL.md lines 169-184 ('Ask these questions in order; stop and wait for each answer before proceeding', followed by 'for each repository' and 'for each named group' sub-loops); corroborated by the same 'ask, wait for the user's answer' pattern at lines 109-114 (clone destination) and the explicit backup/diff/confirm sequence at Phase 5 (lines 204-216).
lower_rungs_attempted: One actor stage per phase, with the whole multi-question interview embedded in one CONTEXT.md turn.
One coarse Work needs_input round-trip per phase, collecting all of a phase's answers together.
One stage per individual question, splitting Phase 4 into a fixed number of stages.
engine_gap.why_each_fails: One actor stage per phase fails because the measured Claude adapter (GAUNTLET D2, confirmed at M4) drives bounded headless `claude -p --output-format stream-json` turns with no TTY/pane; a turn either completes or it does not, so nothing inside one turn can suspend after question 1, wait for an out-of-band answer, and then resume the same reasoning context to ask question 2. A coarse per-phase needs_input round-trip changes the skill's own specified semantics: it requires 'stop and wait for each answer before proceeding' one question at a time so that an early answer (e.g. zero repositories) can end the interview before later questions are even asked; collecting all answers in one round-trip cannot express that early-stop behavior. One stage per individual question is expressible today for the fixed-count parts (project name, defaults, identity, graphify path) but not for the per-repository and per-group loops, whose round count depends on the user's own prior answers -- the current engine requires a workflow's stage list to be a statically pinned, resolved-before-Work-starts sequence (proposal §3.3, 'journal the resolved WorkflowDefinition before execution'), which cannot express a variable number of stages decided at runtime.
engine_gap.minimum_runtime_capability_required: Either (a) a stage class that can emit a structured question, suspend the stage's attempt without ending its trajectory, and resume the same actor context after an API-delivered answer -- an intra-stage needs_input loop distinct from today's whole-Work needs_input -- or (b) a stage-list mechanism that can expand a bounded, data-driven set of question rounds at runtime while remaining journaled and replayable across a restart.
engine_gap.observable_acceptance_test: A workflow stage can ask N sequential, dependent questions where N is determined by earlier answers (e.g., one question per repository the user names), journaling each answer against the same stage attempt and resuming the same actor identity/context after each answer without restarting the stage or losing prior answers, verified across a daemon restart mid-interview.

statement: Before writing the project YAML, sergeant-setup shows a complete preview of the file content and requires explicit confirmation; the file is written only after confirmation.
trigger: all interview answers are collected
outcome: the project YAML is written only after the user has seen and approved the exact content
rationale: Preview-then-confirm, the same pattern already seen for global config.

statement: If a project YAML file already exists when Phase 4 would write a new one, a timestamped backup is created at <name>.yaml.bak.<timestamp> before writing.
trigger: an existing file would be overwritten
outcome: no existing project YAML is lost without a backup

statement: Phase 5 (repair) first validates the existing project YAML with yq; if validation fails, it reports the parse error and stops without proceeding.
trigger: the user wants to modify an existing project YAML
outcome: repair never proceeds against a file whose current state is not understood
rationale: A fail-stop precondition at the start of a distinct checkpoint from Phase 4.

statement: Phase 5 computes and displays a minimal diff between the current file content and the proposed changes before any write.
trigger: the existing YAML validates
outcome: the user can see exactly what would change before approving it

statement: Phase 5 requires explicit confirmation before any write or backup; only after confirmation does it create a timestamped backup and then write the new content. The backup is never created before confirmation, changes are never applied on decline, and the backup is mandatory whenever a write happens -- it is never skipped even if asked.
trigger: a diff has been shown for an existing project YAML
outcome: every applied edit is preceded by both explicit consent and a backup, in that order, with no exception
notes: The 'never skip the backup even if asked' clause is a notably strict, explicitly non-overridable safety rule.

statement: After the project YAML is written, sergeant-setup runs sgt-list, sgt-context <project>, sgt-status <project>, and sgt-sync <project> in that fixed order, stopping at the first failure with its full output and never advancing to the next command until the previous one succeeds.
trigger: the project YAML has been written or repaired
outcome: the new or repaired configuration is proven to actually work end-to-end before later phases run
rationale: A sequential, fail-fast verification checkpoint with clear operator-relevant pass/fail evidence -- a durable checkpoint by the §6.3 test.

statement: For each registered repository, sergeant-setup checks td initialization via `td status --json --work-dir <repo-path>`; if not initialized, it shows and requires explicit consent for `td init --work-dir <repo-path>`, and reports the gap in the final summary if consent is declined.
trigger: the project YAML lists repositories
outcome: every repository ends this phase either td-initialized, explicitly declined-and-reported, or already ok
rationale: A per-repository consent-gated checkpoint with three explicit terminal dispositions.

statement: sergeant-setup never initializes td in a repository that is not registered in the current project YAML.
trigger: Phase 7 iterates repositories for td initialization
outcome: td initialization stays scoped exactly to the project's declared repository set

statement: If treehouse is on PATH, sergeant-setup offers to initialize Treehouse worktree pools with an explicit y/N prompt; it runs only on confirmation, skips silently on decline or absence, and never marks overall setup incomplete because Treehouse was skipped.
trigger: treehouse is present
outcome: Treehouse initialization is strictly optional and its absence never fails the run

statement: If graphify is on PATH and the project YAML declares graphify.output, sergeant-setup offers to run sgt-graphify with an explicit y/N prompt, skips silently on decline, and on a successful run requires both graph.json and GRAPH_REPORT.md to exist at the configured output path.
trigger: graphify is present and configured
outcome: a completed Graphify run is verified by the presence of both its required output artifacts
rationale: The 'require both files to exist' clause is a concrete, checkable completion condition for this checkpoint.

statement: The Phase 10 completion summary lists every checklist item as exactly one of [ok], [skipped], or [issue: <td-id>].
trigger: all prior phases have run or been skipped
outcome: the operator gets one consolidated, unambiguous status line per checklist item

statement: Re-running sergeant-setup after a successful setup must produce the same final state; no phase destroys existing working configuration merely to reach the same end state it already represents.
trigger: sergeant-setup runs against an already-working installation
outcome: the workflow is a true no-op on an already-correct system
rationale: An idempotency guarantee stated for the whole workflow, not one phase -- a defining property of the reusable procedure itself.

statement: cross-repo-work decomposes a requested outcome across the repositories that own it and defines dependency and merge order before any dispatch happens.
trigger: an outcome spans more than one repository
outcome: a reviewed decomposition plan exists before implementation begins
rationale: Recognizable trigger (multi-repo outcome) and bounded outcome (a plan, prior to execution) -- the §6.2 test for a reusable procedure.

statement: cross-repo-work is loaded when sgt-context shows more than one repository owns the requested outcome, not merely because the project contains multiple repositories.
trigger: sgt-context resolves more than one owning repository for the request
outcome: the multi-repo planning workflow only activates when ownership is genuinely split
rationale: A precise negative-trigger boundary preventing over-triggering on any multi-repo project.

statement: cross-repo-work requires load-project to have already resolved repository paths, roles, groups, and instructions.
trigger: cross-repo-work is about to run
outcome: ownership/config context is established before decomposition begins
rationale: Evidence of an ordering dependency between two candidate workflows (load-project before cross-repo-work); relevant to provenance/ordering, not a new checkpoint of cross-repo-work itself.

statement: For each required behavior, cross-repo-work names exactly one owning repository, including a repository only when it must change or produce delivery evidence, and records repo/role/delivers/acceptance for it.
trigger: decomposition begins
outcome: every required behavior has exactly one named owner with a stated observable deliverable and acceptance evidence
rationale: A concrete, checkable output (one owner + acceptance evidence per behavior) makes this a real checkpoint, not incidental prose.

statement: The per-repository ownership record has a fixed shape: repo name, resolved role, the observable behavior or artifact it delivers, and the repo-native command or evidence that proves completion.
trigger: an owning repository is recorded
outcome: every owner record is comparable and machine-checkable
rationale: A structured record template subordinate to the ownership-assignment checkpoint.

statement: Ambiguous repository ownership is resolved using the project graph and existing contracts first; the user is asked only when two repositories could legitimately own a user-visible or durable contract.
trigger: ownership of a behavior is not obvious from role alone
outcome: the user is interrupted only for genuinely contested ownership, not every ambiguity

statement: Dependency edges are created only when one repository's merged or deployed result is required by another, expressed in the prerequisite>dependent notation accepted by sgt-dispatch.
trigger: ownership is assigned
outcome: the dependency graph contains only load-bearing edges, in a syntax the dispatch stage can consume directly
rationale: A distinct checkpoint (producing the dependency graph) with its own bounded outcome, separate from ownership assignment.

statement: Recognized dependency-edge evidence includes: a contract/schema producer preceding its consumers, infrastructure/config preceding runtime that requires it, independent implementations running in parallel once an approved contract exists, and deployment dependency recorded separately from code-merge dependency.
trigger: an edge is being justified
outcome: dependency edges are drawn from a small, principled evidence vocabulary rather than guesswork

statement: Cycles are rejected before dispatch; if a cycle reflects a genuinely coupled contract, cross-repo-work instead defines the contract artifact or compatibility phase that breaks the cycle.
trigger: the drawn dependency edges form a cycle
outcome: no cyclic dependency graph ever reaches dispatch
notes: Cycle detection itself is deterministic and a plausible helper-script candidate (§6.5); the judgment step -- deciding how to break a coupled-contract cycle -- is not.
alternatives_considered: helper (partially applicable: a deterministic cycle-detection check could be a helper script, but resolving a genuine cycle by inventing a compatibility phase requires actor judgment, so the unit as a whole stays stage-context)

statement: cross-repo-work runs sgt-status <project> and records non-main branches, uncommitted changes, ahead/behind state, active worktrees, and preserved workers for every owning repository before planning proceeds.
trigger: ownership and dependencies are being established
outcome: the plan accounts for each owning repository's actual current state
rationale: A distinct evidence-gathering checkpoint prior to writing delivery gates.

statement: cross-repo-work never stashes, resets, switches, or cleans repository state during planning; it either routes an existing canonical branch/worktree into the worker brief or stops for a decision when state conflicts with the requested outcome.
trigger: planning inspects a repository with pre-existing state
outcome: planning is strictly read-only with respect to repository state
notes: A strong, precisely scoped invariant: read-only during planning, with an explicit stop-for-decision escape hatch rather than silent overwrite.
rationale: Scoped specifically to the planning phase of this workflow rather than stated as a system-wide rule.
alternatives_considered: agents-invariant (rejected: explicitly scoped to 'during planning', i.e. this workflow's own phase, not a universal rule)

statement: Every per-repository delivery gate must include: the owning td task (or its creation requirement), the fixed point and preserved source state, repository-specific test/lint/typecheck/build commands, Standards and Spec review sources, PR dependency and deployment order, and any already-approved or still-missing data/security/destructive decisions.
trigger: delivery gates are being defined per repository
outcome: every repository's brief has a complete, checkable gate set before dispatch

statement: The cross-repo plan is complete only when every owning repository has one implementation brief, acceptance evidence, and an acyclic dependency position.
trigger: delivery gates have been drafted for every repository
outcome: the plan's completion condition is explicit and checkable
rationale: A concrete completion condition for the planning checkpoint (§6.3 test).

statement: If the user requested planning only, cross-repo-work stops after returning the briefs, acceptance evidence, and dependency graph, without dispatching or editing any repository; if implementation was requested, it hands off to the dispatch workflow via sgt-dispatch, and the primary session itself never edits several repositories directly.
trigger: planning is complete
outcome: either the plan is returned for review, or execution is handed to a distinct dispatch procedure -- the planning session never becomes a multi-repo editor itself
notes: This is a workflow-to-workflow handoff: cross-repo-work's own completion hands control to the separate dispatch workflow. See the engine-gap recorded against dispatch/SKILL.md (routing to wayfinder/diagnosing-bugs/prototype/tdd/resolving-merge-conflicts) for the fuller evidence trail on informal sub-workflow invocation; this unit is corroborating evidence of the same pattern at the planning/execution boundary.

statement: After dispatched workers finish, cross-repo-work reconciles PR URLs and final heads, required CI and unresolved review threads, merge order from dependency edges, deployment order and cross-repo release notes, and terminal td/fleet state and cleanup eligibility.
trigger: dispatch has completed for the plan's repositories
outcome: the multi-repo outcome is reconciled against every planned gate, not just individual PR existence

statement: cross-repo-work never reports the cross-repo outcome complete until every owning repository has a terminal result or an explicit preserved blocker.
trigger: reconciliation is being evaluated for completeness
outcome: partial completion is never reported as done

statement: dispatch plans and executes a cross-repo task by dispatching one autonomous subagent per repository, each isolated in its own git worktree.
trigger: a task spans multiple repositories and should run in parallel
outcome: each repository's work proceeds independently, isolated from the others
notes: The 'isolated git worktree per unit of work' intent is not obsolete -- sergeant-rs's own runtime/surface.rs already creates host-native git worktrees per Work (proposal §3.6). Only the fan-out to N simultaneous repos under one task, and the tmux-based launch, are new/obsolete respectively (see later units).
rationale: Recognizable trigger (multi-repo parallel task) and bounded outcome (each repo's work isolated and executed) -- the §6.2 test.

statement: dispatch is loaded when a task spans multiple repos and should run in parallel, when the user says something like 'dispatch this' or 'run this across all repos', or when cross-repo-work has already produced a plan the user wants executed.
trigger: one of the listed conditions holds
outcome: the correct workflow (execution, not planning) is selected

statement: dispatch requires load-project (repos/paths/instructions known) and cross-repo-work (repos, dependency order, and per-repo work known, or manually confirmed equivalent) as completed prerequisites.
trigger: dispatch is about to run
outcome: execution never begins without established ownership, paths, and a dependency-ordered plan
rationale: Ordering dependency between three candidate workflows: load-project, cross-repo-work, dispatch.

statement: Before planning from scratch, dispatch checks whether the task already exists in td; if the user's request maps to an open td task, dispatch is invoked with that task id, and the brief, branch name, and full task context are pulled from td automatically, including instructions for the task lifecycle commands the worker must run.
trigger: dispatch is about to plan a task
outcome: existing tracked work is reused rather than re-derived, and the worker's task-lifecycle obligations are pre-populated

statement: Before dispatching, dispatch states the plan explicitly -- which repos, what each does, dependency order, branch, and backend -- and requires that the plan be confirmed as accurate before proceeding.
trigger: a dispatch plan (from a td task or a free-form brief) is ready
outcome: the operator sees and confirms the exact plan before any worktree or agent is created
notes: The illustrated example names 'Backend: local tmux' as a plan field; the underlying durable idea -- state which execution backend each unit will use, as part of the pre-flight plan the operator confirms -- maps onto the new engine's per-stage/per-work harness selection (proposal §11.4/§12.2). The specific value 'local tmux' is obsolete mechanism (superseded per GAUNTLET D2); the field itself is not.

statement: dispatch can be invoked from an existing td task with `sgt-dispatch <project> --td <task-id>`, which auto-detects the owning repo and derives the brief and branch from the task, optionally overriding the repo set explicitly.
trigger: an open td task exists for the work
outcome: a dispatch can be launched from tracked-task identity alone, without re-stating the brief
notes: CLI syntax itself is old-Sergeant mechanism; the conceptual input contract (dispatch accepts a linked tracked-task id, with optional explicit repo-scope override) is durable input-shape evidence.

statement: dispatch can also be invoked from a free-form brief with an explicit repository list, branch name, and dependency string, when no existing td task covers the work.
trigger: no existing td task covers the work
outcome: a dispatch can still be launched from an ad hoc brief with explicit scope, branch, and dependencies
notes: Same mechanism/intent split as the td-task invocation: CLI flags are mechanism, the underlying input contract (explicit repo scope + branch + dependency notation) is durable.

statement: Dispatching a task first generates a durable task identity, then creates an isolated git worktree per target repository at a deterministic sibling path.
trigger: the plan is confirmed
outcome: every dispatched repository has its own isolated, addressable working copy under a durable task identity
notes: Confirmed structurally already present, not obsolete: sergeant-rs's runtime/surface.rs already creates host-native git worktrees per Work (proposal §3.6); what dispatch adds beyond today's engine is doing this N times under one task identity (see the fleet engine-gap below).

statement: Each worker's starting context must durably carry its mission, the merged/resolved agent instructions, dependency notes, and delivery requirements, before the worker begins.
trigger: a worktree has been created for a dispatched repository
outcome: the worker never begins without a complete, self-contained starting brief
rationale: The durable intent (a complete, pinned starting context per unit of work) is exactly what sergeant-rs's pinned WorkflowDefinition / StartRequest context delivery already does structurally (proposal §3.3); see the paired obsolete-mechanism unit on the same source line for the superseded delivery mechanism.

statement: The mechanism for delivering the worker's starting context is a plain Markdown file (.sergeant-brief.md) written directly into the worktree, outside any durable event log.
trigger: a worktree has been created for a dispatched repository
outcome: the worker can read its brief from a well-known file path
notes: Same source line as the paired stage-context unit above; this unit isolates the mechanism, not the intent.
rationale: A loose, unversioned file drop is superseded by sergeant-rs's journaled workflow.bound / StartRequest context delivery (CLAUDE.md 'the journal is the only truth'; proposal §3.3) -- the same starting-context guarantee is already provided as a durable, replayable fact rather than an ordinary worktree file.

statement: The mechanism for launching each dispatched worker is a locally spawned tmux window, one per repository.
trigger: a worktree and brief exist for a dispatched repository
outcome: an agent process is running against that worktree
rationale: Directly superseded per GAUNTLET D2: 'Daemon has no TTY/pane... headless turn sequence -- claude -p --output-format stream-json... Confirmed at M4.' The durable intent (an agent process bound to this worktree) survives via the Claude adapter's headless per-turn model; the tmux-pane launch mechanism does not.

statement: Dispatching a task must create durable, inspectable fleet state describing every worker spawned under that task, at a well-known location.
trigger: workers have been spawned for a task
outcome: the set of workers belonging to one task is durably recorded and later inspectable as a group
notes: See the attached engine-gap: today's Work model owns exactly one Git surface per Work (proposal §3.6); grouping N independent per-repo dispatches under one task/fleet identity, with dependency edges between them, is not representable by the current engine and is the strongest engine-pressure finding in this partition.
rationale: Every lower rung considered either loses the fleet identity itself, loses the ability to enforce declared dependency edges between members, or reproduces the exact 'hidden sub-workflow' pattern §7.7/§10.3 already reject.

engine_gap.behavior: A single logical cross-repository task ('fleet') must durably group N independent per-repository dispatches -- each an isolated git worktree plus its own agent execution -- under one identity, track each member's individual state, honor declared dependency edges between members (e.g. smith-infra>smith), and support fleet-scoped monitoring, response delivery, and cleanup as one durable object, while each member also remains individually retryable/recoverable.
engine_gap.source_evidence: dispatch/SKILL.md line 84 ('Creates fleet state at ~/.local/share/sergeant/fleet/<task-id>/'); dispatch/SKILL.md lines 88-92 (sgt-watch aggregating per-repo .sergeant-status/.sergeant-message/.sergeant-result into one live fleet table); dispatch/SKILL.md lines 149-157 (--deps 'a>b,a>c' dependency notation, with 'the workers themselves are responsible for honoring this' -- i.e. no runtime enforcement today either); dispatch/SKILL.md lines 117-119 (sgt-cleanup <task-id> removing worktrees and fleet state for the whole task at once); cross-repo-work/SKILL.md lines 42-43 (the same prerequisite>dependent notation, produced by planning and consumed by dispatch).
lower_rungs_attempted: Represent the whole cross-repo task as one Work, with per-repo dispatches as ordinary sequential stages of that one Work.
Represent each repository's dispatch as its own independent top-level Work, coordinated only by convention (e.g. a shared task-id string embedded in each Work's metadata).
Represent fan-out and dependency edges purely as authored workflow content: a stage's CONTEXT.md instructs the actor to submit N separate `sgt run` invocations and poll them.
engine_gap.why_each_fails: One Work with per-repo dispatches as stages fails because today's Work owns exactly one Git surface (proposal §3.6, runtime/surface.rs) and one backend/session for the whole run (§3.5); a stage cannot fan out into N independently-progressing, independently-recoverable native harness sessions each in its own worktree, and a single stage's completion is one BackendSignal, not N concurrent ones. N independent top-level Works coordinated only by a shared string fails because the engine itself has no fleet/parent identity to query: dependency edges (smith-infra>smith) cannot be enforced or even observed by the engine, only inferred by an external actor re-reading each Work's state one at a time, and a crash mid-fan-out leaves no journaled record of which Works belong to which fleet or what the intended dependency graph was -- exactly the ambiguity CLAUDE.md's 'ambiguity fails closed' invariant says must not be silently guessed past. Authored-content fan-out (actor-issued `sgt run` calls) is explicitly rejected by §7.7/§10.3: it hides the parent/child relationship from the parent workflow, and dispatch's own contract already requires exactly the visibility that loses (sgt-watch's live per-repo status table, and sgt-respond addressed by both task-id and repo).
engine_gap.minimum_runtime_capability_required: A durable fleet/parent-task identity that groups a fixed or dynamically-declared set of member Works, records declared dependency edges between members, exposes fleet-scoped read views (aggregate status, per-member state) through the API, and supports fleet-scoped operations (respond to one member, cancel/clean up the whole fleet) whose effects are journaled against both the member Work and the fleet identity.
engine_gap.observable_acceptance_test: Submitting one cross-repo task creates one fleet record referencing N member Works with declared dependency edges; the API can list all N members and their states under the fleet id; a dependent member is held (not merely advised) until its declared prerequisite member reaches a terminal successful state, purely from journaled evidence; and canceling or cleaning up the fleet id transitions/removes exactly its N members, verified after a daemon restart mid-fleet.

statement: needs_input and blocked are distinct nonterminal states for a dispatched worker; a worker waiting on CI, review threads, or dependencies stays in_progress unless it actually needs to escalate.
trigger: sgt-watch observes a dispatched worker
outcome: the operator sees a precise nonterminal state rather than an undifferentiated 'still running'
notes: This distinction maps directly onto sergeant-rs's own WorkState enum, which already separates waiting, needs_input, and blocked (CLAUDE.md §3.2) -- confirmation that the existing state vocabulary already matches this corpus's needs, not an engine gap.

statement: When a worker escalates, the coordinator must read its full context, evidence, exact question/blocker, recommendation, and options; obtain an explicit human decision without inferring consequential intent; and deliver that decision to the specific task/repo pair via sgt-respond, which durably writes the response to fleet state before notifying the worker.
trigger: a dispatched worker escalates
outcome: the human decision is fully informed, explicit, durably recorded, and delivered to the correct worker
notes: The final delivery step also 'nudges the recorded local tmux pane when available' -- that notification-delivery detail is obsolete mechanism (tmux pane injection), superseded by the daemon's own process-handle ownership and API-driven wake path; the durable requirement (response is written before the worker is notified) is not.

statement: After a response is delivered, the worker must consume/remove the response, clear its escalation message, log the decision to td, and return to in_progress before continuing.
trigger: a response has been delivered to an escalated worker
outcome: the worker's escalation state is durably cleared and the decision is logged before work resumes
notes: A consume-then-clear-then-resume sequence over ordinary files is exactly the class of adjacent, causally-linked writes CLAUDE.md's 'adjacent-append crash windows' hazard warns about: any implementation of this must tolerate a crash between 'consume the response' and 'clear the message'.

statement: An operator can attach directly to a dispatched worker's session to observe or assist it in real time.
trigger: an operator wants to directly observe or intervene in a live worker
outcome: live, direct observation of an in-progress worker is possible
notes: The mechanism (tmux attach / window switching) is fully obsolete per D2 (daemon has no TTY/pane); the durable intent (real-time observation of a live in-progress worker) is served differently today by the TUI and embedded dashboard (M6).

statement: Reconciliation after all workers finish requires verifying, per repository: pinned-base scope, focused/full validation, separate standards/spec review artifacts, an accessibility review artifact for UI-facing work, zero blocking findings, required CI, and resolved non-outdated review threads; and checking dependency order so infra merges before API before app when there is a runtime dependency.
trigger: all dispatched workers report done
outcome: completion is verified against a fixed, itemized gate list, not merely 'a PR exists'

statement: A fleet is never reconciled or cleaned up merely because every worker has opened a PR; all completion gates must be met.
trigger: every dispatched worker has opened a PR
outcome: PR existence alone never triggers reconciliation/cleanup

statement: Sergeant prefers treehouse for worktree management: a pre-warmed pool of worktrees per repository, leased rather than created fresh, with pooled cleanup.
trigger: worktrees are being provisioned for dispatch
outcome: worktree provisioning can use a faster, pooled mechanism when configured
rationale: An optional, deterministic provisioning optimization layered on top of the durable 'isolated worktree per repo' requirement -- a helper choice, not a new checkpoint.

statement: If a repository has treehouse.toml, dispatch leases a pool worktree, checks out the branch inside it, and returns it via `treehouse return <path>` on cleanup; if not initialized, dispatch falls back to plain `git worktree add` at a deterministic sibling path.
trigger: a worktree is being provisioned for a repository
outcome: worktree provisioning is one of two interchangeable deterministic mechanisms, chosen by per-repo configuration, invisible to the rest of the procedure

statement: The --deps ordering string only expresses that one repository must finish before dependents can merge; enforcing it is left entirely to the dispatched workers reading it out of their own brief.
trigger: a dependency string is declared for a dispatch
outcome: dependency intent is documented, but nothing outside the worker's own judgment enforces it
notes: Directly strengthens the fleet-dependency engine-gap recorded at line 84: the corpus's own text confirms today's mechanism pushes dependency enforcement onto actor judgment reading a text brief rather than any runtime guarantee.

statement: Every dispatched worker pins a fixed point -- normally the merge-base with current origin/main -- and records the base SHA, commit list, and diff scope before implementing anything.
trigger: a worker's session starts
outcome: the worker's later diff and evidence are always measured against a recorded, immutable starting point
notes: Confirms sergeant-rs's own runtime/surface.rs git worktree creation already records a base SHA per work surface (proposal §3.6) -- corroborating evidence that this is genuine required behavior, not incidental old-Sergeant mechanism.

statement: Every dispatched worker triages the full originating td issue/spec/comments and linked material, prior or redundant work, category, and readiness, and explicitly records when no originating spec exists.
trigger: a worker's session starts
outcome: the worker never begins implementation without having read and recorded its own originating context

statement: Before implementation, a worker routes to the canonical engineering skill matching the nature of the work, in a fixed precedence: huge/foggy work surfaces wayfinder/to-spec/to-tickets as an escalation/planning path (never silently executed as implementation); hard bug/performance work loads diagnosing-bugs; uncertain logic/UI work loads prototype; approved implementation loads tdd; merge/rebase conflicts load resolving-merge-conflicts.
trigger: a worker is about to begin implementation
outcome: the correct specialized procedure is selected by judgment about the nature of the work, not assumed to always be plain implementation
notes: The clearest evidence in this partition of real conditional sub-procedure invocation: a worker mid-procedure judges which of several other full durable procedures to run as its own sub-procedure, then presumably returns to finish the dispatch worker contract afterward. See attached engine-gap.
rationale: Judged against §10.3's five-part test for promoting shared context to a shared workflow: the same coherent procedures (diagnosing-bugs, tdd, prototype, resolving-merge-conflicts) recur across many parent contexts; copying their stages into every parent workflow would drift; and each sub-procedure needs its own retry/block/evidence boundaries that shared context cannot grant.

engine_gap.behavior: Mid-procedure, a dispatched worker must conditionally select and fully execute exactly one of several other named durable procedures (wayfinder/to-spec/to-tickets, diagnosing-bugs, prototype, tdd, resolving-merge-conflicts) as a real sub-procedure of its own work item -- with that sub-procedure's own checkpoint/retry/evidence semantics -- chosen by judgment about the nature of the work, then return to and continue the parent dispatch procedure afterward.
engine_gap.source_evidence: dispatch/SKILL.md lines 168-173 (the ordered routing list); dispatch/SKILL.md line 19-21 (cross-repo-work and load-project as completed-workflow prerequisites of dispatch itself, i.e. workflow-before-workflow ordering already exists informally); cross-repo-work/SKILL.md lines 83-85 ('load `dispatch` and execute through `sgt-dispatch`' -- the planning workflow handing off to the execution workflow).
lower_rungs_attempted: Treat the routing list as shared actor context (a @@name reference the worker's stage context includes).
Treat each of the five candidate procedures as a shared helper the worker's stage invokes.
Have the worker silently issue its own `sgt run` for the chosen procedure and poll it to completion before continuing.
engine_gap.why_each_fails: Shared context only lets the actor read guidance text (§10.2); it cannot grant the chosen sub-procedure its own durable checkpoint boundaries, retry, blocked/needs_input state, or evidence -- those exist only if the sub-procedure runs as Sergeant-tracked Work with its own journaled stages, which text inclusion cannot create. Treating the five procedures as helpers fails the §6.5 test directly: a helper is deterministic machinery subordinate to the calling stage's outcome, but diagnosing-bugs, tdd, and prototype are themselves full multi-step, judgment-requiring procedures (proposal §8.2 independently calls diagnosing-bugs 'a strong low-ambiguity reference workflow'), not deterministic subordinate operations. Silent actor-issued `sgt run` is explicitly rejected by §7.7/§10.3: it hides the relationship from the parent workflow, so the parent dispatch procedure has no visibility into the child's stage-level state, no deterministic retry/cancellation reaching into the child, and no parent-aware recovery if the daemon restarts mid-child-run.
engine_gap.minimum_runtime_capability_required: A stage class (or stage attribute) that can invoke a named other workflow as a real child Work chosen from a bounded declared set (or at minimum an explicit judgment-bound choice recorded as evidence) at stage-entry time; the child runs with its own journaled stages/attempts, and on child completion, block, or failure returns control to the parent stage with the child's outcome visible in the parent's trajectory and to parent-aware recovery.
engine_gap.observable_acceptance_test: A workflow stage declares a set of permissible child workflows; when the actor selects one and it runs to completion (or blocks), the parent Work's trajectory shows the child Work's id and terminal outcome; canceling the parent transitions the child; and a daemon restart mid-child-run recovers both parent and child from journaled evidence without an operator having to guess which child, if any, was in flight.

statement: A worker establishes public behavioral seams from td/spec evidence before writing tests; if a consequential seam is undecided, it escalates needs_input rather than guessing.
trigger: a worker is about to define testable seams
outcome: undecided consequential design points are escalated, never silently assumed
notes: Names needs_input explicitly, matching sergeant-rs's existing WorkState -- confirmation, not a gap.

statement: A worker in needs_input or blocked writes an escalation message and notifies the coordinator; on response, it consumes/removes the response, clears the message, logs the decision to td, restores in_progress, and continues -- the durable requirement is that answering a blocked worker always durably restores forward progress, regardless of the underlying file-based transport.
trigger: a worker needs input or is blocked
outcome: the escalation-to-resume cycle always ends with the worker durably back in progress
notes: The .sergeant-message/.sergeant-response file protocol is obsolete mechanism, superseded by the daemon's own journal plus the needs_input/respond API path (CLAUDE.md); the durable requirement -- a blocked/needs_input worker resumes forward progress once answered -- is not.

statement: No-mistakes is run only at an explicit final shipping boundary, never for routine worker completion, prototypes, investigations, documentation drafts, intermediate commits, or remediation loops, unless the user explicitly overrides that default; safety-sensitive work follows a stricter path.
trigger: a worker reaches a candidate shipping boundary
outcome: the expensive shipping gate runs only where it is actually warranted
notes: Overlaps P2's no-mistakes skill's own preconditions; recorded here because it is dispatch's own embedded copy of the rule governing when a dispatched worker may invoke the gate.

statement: Every no-mistakes finding is routed through sgt-no-mistakes-finding into a separate, deduplicated, owning-repo td task; correctness/security/data-integrity/test/ask-user findings are P1 and gated, warning debt is P2, informational debt is P3, and cosmetic/evidence noise is ignored -- and findings are never remediated inside the validation run itself.
trigger: no-mistakes has produced findings
outcome: every actionable finding becomes tracked work at a severity-appropriate priority, and the validation run itself stays read-only with respect to remediation

statement: Independent review runs as separate parallel subagents for the axes named by a shared axis-vocabulary source (standards, spec, readiness, plus a conditional accessibility axis for UI-facing work identified by role/group/description language), each described by guidance reproduced verbatim in the generated brief; the spec axis is explicitly skipped when no spec exists.
trigger: a worker reaches independent review
outcome: review axes, their guidance, and their applicability conditions come from one canonical source rather than being redefined per invocation
notes: Corroborates the P6 helper-map: bin/_sgt-review-axes.sh is a genuine single-source-of-truth shared vocabulary, echoed verbatim in both this skill's generated brief and its consuming router.

statement: When a finding fails to route after parsing, the router retains a sanitized findings artifact under a fixed path and names the exact retry command; the artifact is retried from, never re-generated by re-running the reviewer, and a retained artifact that has not been retried is never deleted.
trigger: a review finding fails to route
outcome: evidence is preserved and addressable rather than silently dropped or expensively re-derived
notes: Strong parallel to CLAUDE.md's evidence-preservation ethos (the journal is the only truth; nothing is silently re-derived when durable evidence already exists).

statement: A stored finding-card revision the router cannot prove it authored is preserved below a superseded-revision separator and the card gains a needs-reconciliation label; only the worker owning the finding may merge the two accounts and remove that label -- the router itself never clears it.
trigger: the router would otherwise overwrite a card revision it did not create
outcome: concurrent writers to the same card never silently clobber each other; reconciliation is an explicit, owned obligation
notes: A genuinely reusable append-then-flag-for-reconciliation concurrency-safety pattern, resembling CLAUDE.md's adjacent-append crash-window class (LESSONS L6).
alternatives_considered: shared-context (noted, not claimed here): this reconciliation-label pattern could generalize beyond findings cards to any concurrently-writable durable record; flagged for helper-map/shared-context-map consideration rather than asserted as already-generalized in the corpus.

statement: Findings sharing the same originating run, head, owning module, and root cause share one serialized remediation worker/branch; before merging that group, native tests and independent re-reviews verifying mutation-before-validation, partial-publication/rollback, and identity/provenance are rerun; after two remediation cycles, fix dispatch stops and an architectural/root-cause review plus a human decision is required.
trigger: multiple findings share a root cause
outcome: remediation is deduplicated, re-verified before merge, and escalates to a human after bounded retries rather than looping indefinitely

statement: A worker writes .sergeant-result and sets its status to done only after every completion gate has passed; a failed status with an exact reason is reserved specifically for an unrecoverable terminal failure.
trigger: a worker reaches a terminal outcome
outcome: the terminal status distinguishes verified success from unrecoverable failure, and neither is asserted prematurely
notes: The file-based status mechanism is obsolete; the durable contract it encodes -- an explicit terminal-state distinction requiring all gates before success, mirroring WorkState's completed/failed distinction and the 'completed and canceled Work are absorbing' invariant -- is not.

statement: If a canonical skill referenced by the routing table cannot be loaded, the generated brief's own embedded rules for that phase remain mandatory regardless.
trigger: a canonical skill named by the routing table is unavailable
outcome: the phase's requirements still apply even without the specialized skill loaded
rationale: A degradation/fallback policy for the workflow-composition pattern discussed in the attached engine-gap: today, the fallback is duplicated prose in the generated brief rather than an engine-owned default.

statement: Dispatching from a free-form brief creates exactly one td task per target repository before spawning any worker; if td is unavailable, task creation fails, generated metadata cannot be injected, or any selected repo fails to get a task, the whole dispatch aborts before spawning any worker and rolls back the generated tasks.
trigger: a free-form dispatch is being launched
outcome: task creation for a multi-repo dispatch is all-or-nothing, never partially committed before any agent starts
notes: An atomicity/rollback invariant on the pre-flight side of dispatch -- resembles the adjacent-append crash-window concern class (commit fully or roll back before any irreversible side effect).

statement: Recovering a stuck, stale, or orphaned dispatched worker is done only through sgt-respond or an equivalent explicit action; a worker is never marked done manually, and a retry writes both the result and the done status only after every completion gate passes.
trigger: a worker appears stuck, stale, or orphaned
outcome: recovery never fabricates a successful terminal state; it either delivers an explicit response or nothing changes
notes: Corroborates the 'ambiguity fails closed'/no-guessing invariant already present in sergeant-rs (CLAUDE.md §4.3): old Sergeant's own troubleshooting guidance already refuses to let an operator hand-mark uncertain state as done.

statement: load-project resolves Sergeant project ownership, configuration, and paths before any work begins.
trigger: a project must be resolved before other work proceeds
outcome: repository ownership, config, and paths are established as a precondition
rationale: Recognizable trigger (a project needs resolving) and bounded outcome (context established) -- §6.2 test.

statement: load-project is loaded when a project is named, registered, edited, synced, or graphed, or when repository ownership is not already established by sgt-context output.
trigger: one of the listed conditions holds
outcome: the correct workflow (context resolution) is selected

statement: If the project name is unknown, load-project runs sgt-list and requires an exact registered name before proceeding.
trigger: the project name is not already known
outcome: work never proceeds against a guessed or partial project name

statement: load-project runs sgt-context <project> and records the owning repositories, resolved absolute paths and clone state, group membership and roles, instructions inherited in defaults-then-group-then-repository order, and any configured Graphify output and included groups.
trigger: the project name is known
outcome: a complete, resolved context snapshot exists for downstream workflows to consume
notes: The defaults -> group -> repository instruction-layering order is precise, reusable evidence -- the same layering concept named in docs/what-is-sergeant.md (P1); a strong shared-context-map candidate.

statement: A raw project YAML is read directly only when a required field is absent from the resolved sgt-context output.
trigger: sgt-context output is missing a needed field
outcome: the resolved context view is always preferred over the raw source file, used only as a fallback

statement: A missing required repository is synced only once the requested work actually requires it, via sgt-sync <project>; the workflow stops if cloning or pulling fails.
trigger: a required repository is not present locally
outcome: repositories are fetched lazily and on failure the workflow does not proceed on an incomplete checkout

statement: Completion evidence for load-project is the sgt-context block showing every owning repository as cloned, plus the instructions and paths that will govern execution.
trigger: context resolution finishes
outcome: there is one concrete, checkable artifact proving the checkpoint is satisfied
rationale: An explicit completion-evidence definition is itself strong evidence this is a real durable checkpoint (§6.3 test).

statement: Registering or editing a project starts by reading docs/schema.md and, when editing, the existing YAML.
trigger: the user asks to add or change a project
outcome: the schema and any existing content are read before any change is proposed

statement: Project YAML is written only to ~/.config/sergeant/<project>.yaml, and credentials, tokens, or secret values are never placed in it.
trigger: a project YAML is being written
outcome: project config never becomes a place secrets are stored
notes: A no-secrets-in-authored-artifacts rule that recurs independently in the wiki skill (storage-ownership and digest-review rules); a genuine cross-workflow invariant candidate.
alternatives_considered: agents-invariant (considered: 'never place secrets in a versioned/plain-text authored artifact' recurs at least three times across this partition alone -- see wiki/SKILL.md storage-ownership and digest-review units -- but each instance is stated locally to its own artifact type here, so kept as stage-context per-file pending a cross-partition merge at classification-ledger stage)

statement: Repository paths in project YAML are always either absolute or relative to the global dev_root.
trigger: a repository entry is being written
outcome: repository paths are always resolvable without ambiguity

statement: A single project-level graphify.output path, located outside any source repository, is configured when project Graphify is required.
trigger: project Graphify is required
outcome: graph output never lands inside a source repository

statement: After writing project YAML, load-project runs sgt-list and requires the project to appear exactly once, then runs sgt-context <project> and requires every edited field needed by agents to appear in the resolved output.
trigger: project YAML has been written or edited
outcome: the write is verified end-to-end, not merely assumed to have parsed

statement: sgt-sync <project> runs only when repositories actually need cloning or refreshing, not unconditionally after every edit.
trigger: project YAML has been verified
outcome: sync is triggered by actual need, not by habit

statement: If validation fails after a registration/edit, load-project restores the prior YAML or leaves the new file uncommitted, and reports the exact command error.
trigger: post-write verification fails
outcome: a failed edit never leaves the project in a half-written, unverified state

statement: docs/schema.md remains the single source of truth for project YAML fields; agent instructions never duplicate its field reference.
trigger: project schema is being documented or referenced
outcome: there is exactly one authoritative place to look up project YAML fields
rationale: A stable, broadly-scoped documentation-authority rule independent of any one stage -- the §6.1 test.

statement: Project Graphify is run by reading the configured output path from sgt-context, stopping to request or add that path if unconfigured, then running sgt-graphify <project>.
trigger: a project architecture question or explicit graph-update request arises
outcome: Graphify never runs without a validated project-level output location

statement: graphify query is used for focused questions; GRAPH_REPORT.md is read for broad architecture, community, and god-node context.
trigger: an architecture question needs answering
outcome: the right query surface is chosen for the question's scope

statement: Generated project graph output is never published inside an owning source repository.
trigger: Graphify has run successfully
outcome: graph output stays a separate, disposable projection, never mixed into source history
notes: Echoes the proposal's own 'projections remain disposable' invariant (§4.9), independently corroborated by this corpus.

statement: If a named project is unregistered, load-project stops and asks whether to register it, rather than proceeding on an assumed project.
trigger: the requested project is unregistered
outcome: no work proceeds against a project that does not yet exist

statement: If a required repository entry has no clone URL, load-project stops with the repository name and the missing field named explicitly.
trigger: a required repository lacks a URL
outcome: the operator gets a precise, actionable error rather than a downstream sync failure

statement: If a required executable is missing, load-project reports the executable and a platform-neutral installation requirement, and never invents a fallback parser.
trigger: a required executable is absent
outcome: missing tooling is reported honestly instead of being silently worked around with invented parsing logic
notes: A precise anti-invention rule, matching this repo's own measure-don't-assume doctrine (LESSONS L1).

statement: If sgt-context and the raw project YAML disagree, the sgt-context failure is treated as blocking and the YAML is preserved for diagnosis.
trigger: resolved context and raw source disagree
outcome: disagreement between resolved and raw sources is never silently resolved by picking one

statement: Stale graph output is refreshed via sgt-graphify only when architecture work actually requires it or the user explicitly requests it, never automatically.
trigger: graph output is known to be stale
outcome: regeneration is need-driven, not automatic or habitual

statement: sergeant-help answers Sergeant installation, setup, usage, skills, and troubleshooting questions strictly from repository-owned documentation.
trigger: a Sergeant informational question is asked
outcome: the answer is grounded in repository-owned docs, not invented
rationale: Recognizable trigger (an informational question) and bounded outcome (a documentation-grounded answer) -- §6.2 test.

statement: sergeant-help is loaded when the user asks what Sergeant is, how to install/configure/use it, where skills come from, how to run a command/workflow, or how to diagnose a Sergeant error.
trigger: one of the listed question types is asked
outcome: the read-only help workflow, not an executing workflow, is selected

statement: sergeant-help is never used as a substitute for load-project, cross-repo-work, dispatch, or wiki once the user has actually requested execution of those procedures.
trigger: the user has requested execution, not just an explanation
outcome: read-only help never silently absorbs a request meant for an executing workflow
rationale: Crystallizes the read-only-help vs. executing-workflow boundary already implied by sergeant-setup's own 'use sergeant-help instead' notes -- consistent design intent across the partition.

statement: sergeant-help maps question categories to one primary document each: product/deployment model, install/first-project, skill sources, direct/dispatch workflows and commands, errors/stale-workers/auth/gates/cleanup, project YAML fields, and agent execution policy.
trigger: a question needs classifying
outcome: the search for an answer starts from the single most authoritative document for that question's category
rationale: A deterministic lookup table the actor consults, not itself a judgment-requiring checkpoint.

statement: Answering a question first classifies it against the documentation map, then reads the primary document before searching broadly.
trigger: a question arrives
outcome: the most authoritative source is consulted before any broad search

statement: For terms not resolved by the primary document, sergeant-help searches repository documentation and skills with a case-insensitive ripgrep over Markdown files scoped to README.md, docs, and skills.
trigger: the primary document does not resolve a term
outcome: the search stays scoped to the repository's own documented behavior, not general knowledge

statement: For architectural questions where a configured Sergeant graph exists, sergeant-help runs graphify query and uses cited source locations in the answer.
trigger: the question is architectural and a graph is configured
outcome: architectural answers are backed by cited, queryable graph evidence

statement: For flag or argument questions, sergeant-help runs --help only when the command supports it; otherwise it inspects the command's actual emitted usage/error contract and its tests.
trigger: a flag or argument question is asked
outcome: the answer comes from the command's real, observed contract rather than assumed documentation
notes: Directly parallels this repo's own measure-don't-assume doctrine (LESSONS L1: 'measure the claude CLI'); this corpus independently encodes the same value for its own command surface.

statement: Answers state the exact command, required preconditions, expected evidence, and links to repository-relative documentation paths.
trigger: an answer is being formulated
outcome: every answer is independently actionable and independently verifiable

statement: When sources disagree, precedence is: command behavior/tests/supported --help output for released syntax, then AGENTS.md for always-on execution/safety policy, then the trigger-loaded skill for its own procedure, then docs/schema.md for project fields, then user documentation for walkthroughs.
trigger: documentation sources disagree
outcome: disagreement is resolved by a fixed, principled precedence order rather than by whichever source was read last
notes: A precise evidence hierarchy for this corpus, directly analogous in shape to the governing proposal's own evidence hierarchy (§2: implementation > contracts/ledger/lessons > vendored corpus > external docs > proposal).

statement: sergeant-help explicitly states when a behavior is undocumented or contradictory rather than inventing a command, flag, state transition, or safety guarantee.
trigger: a question cannot be answered from grounded sources
outcome: an honest gap is reported instead of a fabricated answer
rationale: A broadly-scoped anti-invention rule stated independently of any one stage, matching the §6.1 test.

statement: The help response format is a fixed template: Answer, Command (when applicable), Requires, Verify, Docs -- with fields omitted when they do not apply.
trigger: an answer is being delivered
outcome: every answer has a consistent, scannable, evidence-linked shape

statement: Destructive operations are kept out of examples unless the documentation itself requires confirmation for them and the user explicitly requested them.
trigger: an example command is being included in an answer
outcome: help output never casually demonstrates a destructive action
notes: Same consent-before-destructive-action family as the setup/dispatch consent-gate pattern, applied here to documentation output rather than live execution.

statement: If the primary document for a question is missing, sergeant-help reports its expected path and stops before guessing.
trigger: the mapped primary document does not exist
outcome: a missing authoritative source is reported, never silently worked around

statement: If observed command behavior differs from documentation, sergeant-help reports the mismatch, trusts tested/released behavior or supported --help output over the stale doc, and creates or suggests a documentation task.
trigger: docs and observed behavior disagree
outcome: the operator gets both the correct current answer and a path to fixing the stale doc
notes: Another direct instance of the measure-over-assume doctrine already noted for lines 41-42.

statement: If a question actually requires project ownership context, sergeant-help loads load-project and runs sgt-context rather than answering from memory.
trigger: a question needs project-specific context
outcome: help defers to the workflow that actually resolves that context

statement: If a question actually requires implementation or fleet mutation, sergeant-help hands off to the owning procedural skill; help itself remains strictly read-only.
trigger: a question actually requires a mutating action
outcome: sergeant-help never performs or triggers mutation itself
notes: Reinforces the read-only-help vs. executing-workflow boundary already recorded at lines 12-13.

statement: wiki maintains Sergeant's automatic activity captures and a curated daily session digest.
trigger: wiki output needs to be ingested, backfilled, regenerated, inspected, or changed
outcome: raw captures and curated pages stay distinct and both remain maintained
rationale: Recognizable trigger and bounded outcome -- §6.2 test.

statement: wiki is loaded only for explicit ingest/backfill/regenerate/inspect/change requests on wiki output; routine dispatch, notification, and cleanup commands write automatic captures without any coordinator action or wiki-skill invocation.
trigger: the request is an explicit wiki-management action versus routine command execution
outcome: wiki is not loaded merely because some other command happens to write a capture as a side effect
notes: Captures are produced as a side effect of dispatch/notify/cleanup, not by running the wiki workflow -- the wiki workflow itself only governs curated digestion of those captures.

statement: Automatic activity captures live under ~/wiki/.captures/, written by Sergeant commands; curated pages live under ~/wiki/, governed by ~/wiki/SCHEMA.md; wiki-daily-digest reads session history plus captures and writes the curated pages.
trigger: wiki storage is being read or written
outcome: raw evidence and curated narrative are stored in clearly separated, independently governed locations
notes: The capture/curated-page separation maps onto sergeant-rs's own journal-vs-projection separation: captures are analogous to raw journaled events, curated pages to a disposable derived projection (proposal §3.9, §4.9).
rationale: A durable storage-boundary convention used by both the automatic-capture producers and the digest consumer -- reusable across multiple commands/workflows, not local to one stage.

statement: Curated wiki pages never contain raw prompts, response bodies, credentials, tokens, or secrets; only task, repository, PR, merge, decision, and blocker facts are preserved, and only when the wiki schema permits them.
trigger: content is being written to a curated page
outcome: curated pages can never leak raw conversational or secret material
notes: Third independent instance in this partition of a no-secrets-in-authored-artifacts rule (see load-project/SKILL.md lines 39-40 and the digest-review rule below) -- strong cross-workflow invariant evidence.
alternatives_considered: agents-invariant (considered: the rule recurs across at least three source files in this partition alone, but each instance names a different artifact type -- project YAML, curated wiki pages, digest previews -- so classified per-instance as shared-context pending a cross-partition merge rather than asserted as one global rule here)

statement: sgt-dispatch, sgt-notify, and sgt-cleanup each own creation of one capture type: fleet-launch metadata, escalation/terminal-outcome plus PR URL, and worktree/fleet cleanup with final status, respectively.
trigger: one of those three commands runs
outcome: each capture type has exactly one owning producer command, unambiguously
rationale: A lookup table of capture responsibility, directly corresponding to three P6 bin/ commands (sgt-dispatch, sgt-notify, sgt-cleanup).

statement: A missing capture is fixed by reproducing the owning command in a fixture or fixing its capture adapter; a missing automatic capture is never hand-synthesized as a substitute.
trigger: an expected capture is missing
outcome: capture evidence is always genuinely produced by its owning command, never fabricated after the fact
notes: Strong parallel to CLAUDE.md's own evidence-integrity doctrine: never fabricate what should have been recorded; fix the producer instead.
rationale: Recorded as workflow-local context here since evidence is specific to this corpus's capture mechanism, though the underlying anti-fabrication principle is broader.

statement: The daily digest is run with one of three modes matching the requested range: --date YYYY-MM-DD, --since YYYY-MM-DD, or --dry-run for either.
trigger: a digest run is requested
outcome: the digest's scope is always explicit and matches exactly what was requested

statement: The digest schema (~/wiki/SCHEMA.md) is read before changing digest behavior or curated structure.
trigger: digest logic or curated structure is about to change
outcome: changes are made with the governing schema in hand, not from memory

statement: --dry-run is run first whenever regenerating an existing day or changing digest logic, before any non-dry run.
trigger: an existing day is being regenerated or digest logic changed
outcome: a preview always precedes a real write in these higher-risk cases
notes: The same preview-before-write discipline already seen in sergeant-setup's config/YAML writes.

statement: The proposed session page is inspected for secret material, duplicate entities, incorrect PR/task outcomes, and unresolved generation errors before it is accepted.
