trigger: a dry-run preview has been produced
outcome: a generated page is human-reviewed against four specific risk categories before being made real
notes: Fourth independent instance in this partition of secret-content vigilance (alongside load-project's YAML rule and wiki's own storage-ownership rule) -- reinforces the cross-workflow invariant evidence.

statement: The non-dry-run digest command is only run once the dry-run preview satisfies the schema.
trigger: a dry-run preview has been reviewed
outcome: curated pages are only ever written from a preview that already passed review

statement: After a real digest run, ~/wiki/sessions/YYYY-MM-DD.md must exist and be linked from ~/wiki/index.md.
trigger: a real digest run has completed
outcome: the digest's completion condition is a concrete, checkable pair of filesystem facts
rationale: A concrete completion-evidence definition -- §6.3 test.

statement: The schema-required ingest log entry is appended or verified after every digest run.
trigger: a real digest run has completed
outcome: the ingest log stays complete and accurate for every run

statement: The digest must synthesize outcomes, decisions, blockers, and next state; it must never reproduce the conversation as a transcript.
trigger: digest content is being generated
outcome: curated pages stay synthesized and durable, never a raw transcript dump

statement: Installing or expanding a scheduler for the digest (e.g. a macOS launchd job running it daily) is treated as a separate task from the digest itself, with the job definition, executable path, environment, last exit status, and generated page all verified before scheduling is reported complete.
trigger: recurring/scheduled digest execution is requested
outcome: scheduling is verified as a real, working external trigger, not merely configured and assumed to work
notes: The corpus explicitly delegates scheduling itself to the OS (launchd) rather than claiming Sergeant must own it -- this is the lower rung actually succeeding for a recurring-execution need, so no engine-gap is recorded here.
rationale: The runtime capability question (must Sergeant itself own scheduled/recurring triggering?) is explicitly answered 'no' by this source: the skill treats an OS-level scheduler invoking the same command Sergeant already exposes as sufficient, so this is not promoted to engine-gap.
alternatives_considered: engine-gap (considered and rejected): the source text itself resolves recurring execution via an external OS scheduler invoking an ordinary command, which is a working lower rung, not a failing one.

statement: If the digest schema is missing or unreadable, wiki stops without writing any curated pages.
trigger: the schema cannot be read
outcome: no curated content is ever written against an unknown or absent schema

statement: If a dry run contains secrets, wiki stops, records only the affected source class (not the secret itself), and fixes redaction before retrying.
trigger: a dry-run preview contains secret material
outcome: the failure is recorded without itself leaking the secret, and is fixed before any retry
notes: Fifth instance of secret-handling vigilance in this partition; also notable that even the failure record itself must avoid leaking the secret.

statement: If PR or td state cannot be resolved, the outcome is marked unresolved rather than having completion inferred.
trigger: PR or td state is unresolvable
outcome: an unknown outcome is recorded as unknown, never guessed as complete
notes: Direct corroboration of the 'ambiguity fails closed' invariant already present in sergeant-rs (CLAUDE.md §4.3) from an independent source in this corpus.

statement: An existing curated page is never overwritten with a version containing less information; the existing page is preserved and the rejected update is reported.
trigger: a regenerated page would contain less information than the existing one
outcome: curated content is monotonically preserved, never regressed by an automatic overwrite

statement: If the index update fails, the generated page itself is kept, its exact path is reported, and the digest is left explicitly marked incomplete.
trigger: updating ~/wiki/index.md fails after a page was generated
outcome: a partial success (page written, index not updated) is reported precisely rather than silently swallowed or silently treated as full success
